sources.cite: ANA and NCSBN. National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation (effective 2019-04-01)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11 (primary PDF, ANA copy). Delegation is allowing a delegatee to perform a specific nursing activity outside their traditional role; assignment is routine care within an authorized scope. Five rights: right task, right circumstance ('The health condition of the patient must be stable'), right person, right directions and communication (specific to the patient, the nurse and the delegatee), right supervision and evaluation. The licensed nurse cannot delegate activities that require clinical reasoning, nursing judgment or critical decision making; keeps overall accountability; must follow up with the delegatee and the patient and stay available; delegation decisions weigh the stability and predictability of the patient's condition.

Read 2026-11-11 (primary PDF). 'Delegate and supervise care of client provided by others (e.g., LPN/VN, assistive personnel, other RNs)'; 'Prioritize the delivery of client care based on acuity'; 'Organize workload to manage time effectively'.

The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles (nurse managers coordinate care, delegate and support staff development; delegate by role and competence keeping accountability; conflict resolution within teams).

brief.situation: 07:00 on a medical-surgical unit. You are the charge nurse. One RN called in sick, so the day team is you, Priya (RN, 12 years), Sam (RN, new graduate, three weeks off orientation), Lena (LPN, floating from another unit) and Marco (nursing assistant). Make the assignments, then lead the shift.
handover: Bed 2, Mr. Ito, 58, day 1 after a hip replacement: since 06:30 heart rate 112 and SpO2 91% on room air, newly anxious. Night shift was about to call the provider.
Bed 4, Mrs. Grant, 82, dementia, stable: bath, feeding help, vital signs every 4 hours. Bed 5, Mr. Lopez, 66, stable diabetes: scheduled medications and a simple dressing.

Bed 7: an admission from the emergency department at 07:30 (cellulitis, IV antibiotics). Bed 8, Ms. Ford: discharge at 09:00 with new anticoagulant teaching. Bed 9, Mr. Dunn: a unit of red cells due at 08:00; unit policy says only RNs hang blood, and Sam has never done it without his preceptor.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Assign, delegate with clear directions, then follow up: your team will come to you with problems as the morning goes on.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. The case ends at 08:30, then a debrief scores what you did.

FLAG: authored. Lena collects data and reports it; an RN assesses him about 45 min in.

lead.question: Explain your assignments and delegation: who has the unstable client and why, what you delegated with what directions, how you supported your team, and who stays accountable.

parts.label: Assignment and delegation
parts.criteria: Gives the unstable, unpredictable client (Bed 2) to the experienced RN or assesses him personally, never to the LPN or assistant; keeps assessment, teaching and transfusion with RNs as policy requires; delegates routine, stable tasks to the assistant with specific directions and report limits; names the five rights; states that the delegating nurse stays accountable and follows up.
parts.modelAnswer: Mr. Ito is unstable and unpredictable, so he goes to Priya, who sees him first, or I assess him myself; he is not delegated or assigned to the LPN, and Marco does not 'check on him'. Marco gets stable, routine tasks for Beds 4 and 5 with exact numbers to report at once. Lena takes Bed 5's medications and dressing within her scope; blood stays with RNs per policy. I stay accountable for what I delegate, so I check back with Marco and the nurses.

parts.label: Leading the team
parts.criteria: Raises the staffing gap with the house supervisor early; listens to the RN's safety concern and rebalances instead of dismissing it; develops the new graduate by pairing him for the transfusion rather than leaving him alone or taking it over.
parts.modelAnswer: The sick call goes to the house supervisor at 07:00. If Priya says her load is unsafe, I listen and move the admission to myself. Sam has never hung blood alone, so he does it with Priya for the check and the first 15 minutes and we debrief after: safe for Mr. Dunn and a step forward for Sam.

Marco: vital signs, baths and breakfast for Beds 4 and 5, with the exact values to report at once. Lena: Bed 5's medications and dressing.

collapse.headline: The unstable client collapsed
collapse.body: Find who had Bed 2, how long it took an RN to reach him, and whether anyone was asked to 'check on him' who could not assess. An unstable client stays with an RN who sees him first: the right circumstance for delegation is a stable client.

ledWell.headline: Right person, right task, a team that knew what to do
ledWell.body: The unstable client with an experienced RN, routine work delegated with specific directions, blood with an RN and the new graduate supported, a concern heard, help asked for, and follow-up. That is the expert path.

ledLate.headline: Through the morning, by a slower route
ledLate.body: Bed 2 is treated, but check who had him and how fast an RN arrived, what Marco was told, who hung the blood, how Sam and Priya were answered, and whether the staffing office heard.

time_up.body: The case ran to its hard stop.

scoring.modelReasoning: A charge nurse coordinates care, delegates and develops the team. The unstable, unpredictable client (Bed 2: tachycardic, hypoxic, newly anxious after surgery) goes to the experienced RN, who sees him first, or the charge nurse assesses him; he is not assigned to the LPN, and the assistant is never asked to judge whether he is okay, because assessment and clinical judgment cannot be delegated (right circumstance, right task). Routine care of stable clients goes to the assistant with specific directions and the values to report at once (right directions and communication), and the charge nurse follows up (right supervision and evaluation), staying accountable. Unit policy keeps blood with RNs; the new graduate who has never hung blood alone is paired with an experienced RN and debriefed (right person, professional development). When an RN says her load is unsafe, listen and rebalance; and raise the sick call with the house supervisor early.

fiveRights.explain: The national guidelines' right circumstance says the patient's health condition must be stable, and delegation decisions weigh how stable and predictable the condition is. Assessment and judgment stay with the licensed nurse.
